questions.q: Where had Toad spent the night at the start of this chapter?
choices: In a hollow tree
In a farmer's barn
On the railway train
In the prison cell
questions.evidence: The front door of the hollow tree faced eastwards

questions.q: How did Toad feel when he woke and remembered everything?
choices: Joyful, because he was free
Terrified that he would be caught
Sad, lonely and homesick
Angry at the kind engine-driver
questions.evidence: The word and the thought alone were worth fifty blankets.

questions.q: What story did Toad tell the barge-woman to get a ride?
choices: He was a washerwoman off to help a married daughter
He was a lost traveller from abroad looking for an inn
He was a farmer's wife taking eggs to the market
He was an old friend of the barge-woman's husband
questions.evidence: Here's my married daughter, she sends off to me post-haste

questions.q: Why did Toad's boasting about loving washing get him into trouble?
choices: The barge-woman asked him to do her washing
The barge-woman wanted to hire his twenty girls
The barge-woman reported him to the police
The barge-woman asked to see his own laundry
questions.evidence: put them through the wash-tub as we go along

choices: Badly; the clothes stayed dirty and he kept losing the soap
Very well; the barge-woman praised his fine, careful work
He refused to wash anything at all and sat sulking
He washed everything perfectly, but very slowly
questions.evidence: lost the soap, for the fiftieth time

questions.q: The barge-woman said she thought Toad was "a humbug all along." What is a humbug?
choices: A fake who pretends to be something he is not
A very hard worker who never stops to rest
A kind of buzzing insect found on boats
A brave hero who saves people in trouble
questions.evidence: I thought you must be a humbug all along

questions.q: What did the barge-woman do after she discovered Toad was a toad?
choices: Flung him into the canal
Locked him in the cabin
Called loudly for her husband
Gave him a hot breakfast
questions.evidence: Toad found himself flying through the air

questions.q: How did Toad get his revenge on the barge-woman?
choices: He untied her horse and rode away on it
He sank her barge in the middle of the canal
He stole her washing and threw it away
He told the police all about her
questions.evidence: unfastened the towrope and cast off, jumped lightly on the horse's back

questions.q: What did Toad finally get from the gipsy in exchange for the horse?
choices: Six and sixpence and a big breakfast of stew
Four shillings, a pair of old boots and some bread
A grey donkey and a little painted cart
A ride home to Toad Hall in the caravan
questions.evidence: counted out six shillings and sixpence into Toad's paw

questions.q: Toad wondered whether it would be easier to fight the gipsy or "cajole" him. What does "cajole" mean?
choices: To coax or sweet-talk someone into something
To run away from someone as fast as possible
To trick someone using some kind of magic
To pay someone a great deal of money
questions.evidence: easier to fight him or cajole him

questions.q: After his breakfast, what did Toad do that showed how conceited he had become?
choices: Made up and sang a song praising himself
Wrote a polite thank-you letter to the gipsy
Went straight home to apologize to his friends
Hid quietly in a ditch until nightfall
questions.evidence: It was perhaps the most conceited song that any animal ever composed.

questions.q: Why did Toad collapse when he saw the motor-car coming?
choices: It was the very car he had stolen from the Red Lion Hotel
It was a police car full of constables looking for him
It came round the bend and nearly ran him over
He was too hungry and tired to stand any longer
questions.evidence: the very one he had stolen out of the yard of the Red Lion Hotel

questions.q: What did the gentlemen in the car think had happened to Toad?
choices: That a poor washerwoman had fainted in the road
That a toad had escaped from the prison nearby
That a thief was hiding by the side of the road
That a little child was lost and needed help
questions.evidence: a washerwoman apparently--who has fainted in the road

questions.q: What did Toad ask for after being moved to the front seat?
choices: To try driving the car
To be taken to Toad Hall
To be let out at the village
Something hot to eat
questions.evidence: let me try and drive the car for a little

questions.q: How did the car ride end?
choices: Toad crashed the car through a hedge into a horse-pond
Toad drove all the way home to the gates of Toad Hall
The gentlemen stopped the car and tied Toad up with rope
The car ran out of petrol on a lonely country road
questions.evidence: the wheels of the car were churning up the thick mud of a horse-pond

questions.q: What lesson does Toad keep failing to learn in this chapter?
choices: His boasting keeps landing him in trouble
He should never trust a horse he does not know
He should always travel by train, not by car
He should learn to swim much better in rivers
questions.evidence: What a CONCEITED and heedless ass!

questions.q: How did Toad end up in the river?
choices: Running from the police, he ran blindly into it
He jumped in on purpose to wash the mud off
The barge-woman caught him and threw him in again
He fell off the gipsy's horse into the water
questions.evidence: in his blind panic he had run straight into the river

questions.q: Whose face did Toad see in the dark hole in the river bank?
choices: The Water Rat's
The Mole's
The Badger's
The barge-woman's

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Toad's tricks and narrow escapes on the way home
Rat and Mole searching the river for little Portly
Toad's trial in court and his long prison sentence
Badger making a plan to win back Toad Hall
questions.evidence: But his pride was shortly to have a severe fall.
